subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown abort managed active runs and exec child processes before the watchdog, or preserve background/yielded exec sessions unless an explicit restart or kill path requests cancellation?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve active/background work on normal stop, so changing this is an operator-safety and product contract decision rather than a mechanical bug patch.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes before the watchdog, with a documented exception for any background process class maintainers choose to preserve.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep SIGTERM/SIGINT from aborting active/background exec work and treat this as a diagnostics/docs issue instead of a runtime cancellation change.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines the process-control contract, then reuse that contract for gateway shutdown.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes before the watchdog, with a documented exception for any background process class maintainers choose to preserve.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history across process supervisor and process-tool surfaces and is already in the issue timeline.
